name: lake
desc: A gentle young man in his late twenties: the village lamplighter. Tousled wavy brown hair, soft warm brown eyes, a warm boyish friendly face, a calm kind manner. He wears a mid-thigh-length charcoal dark-grey HOODED COAT (hood down at the back of the neck) worn OPEN down the front with no belt, its two front edges hanging straight down flat and close against his sides. It has proper set-in SLEEVES on both arms ending at the wrists. A small brass flame-shaped clasp at the throat. The open coat shows a white band-collar shirt and, over it, a fitted SCARLET RED-ORANGE vest (the colour of a lit flame) with cord X-lacing down the front. Brown pants, brown boots. No chest strap, no bag, nothing held in either hand. No part of the garment flares or stands out into empty space.
sheetHint: same face, tousled wavy brown hair, warm boyish late-twenties face, open charcoal hooded coat with proper sleeves on both arms hanging straight and close at his sides, brass flame-shaped clasp at the throat, white band-collar shirt and a scarlet red-orange X-laced vest beneath, brown pants, brown boots, no chest strap, hands empty

expressions.happy: a bright open smile, eyes lit up
expressions.worried: brows knit, small anxious frown, eyes glancing aside
expressions.determined: firm set jaw, focused eyes, faint confident smirk
expressions.tender: soft eyes, small warm smile, head fractionally tilted — the look of giving someone their name back

turnaround.extraNote: THE GARMENT IS A COAT, NOT A CAPE, and that is a MODELLING requirement rather than a style preference (2026-08-02, measured — see _capeVerdict). Sleeves are set-in on both arms so the arms bind to the ARM joints. The coat is worn OPEN (user pick 2026-08-02) and its two front edges must hang STRAIGHT DOWN close against his sides — an open coat's front panels flank the torso right beside the arms, which is the cape's failure geometry at half scale, and the only thing keeping them binding to the spine is staying within a fold's thickness of the body. If char_intake reports those panels arm-weighted, the fallback is to belt the coat closed (art kept at turnaround-cape-retired/front-belted-superseded.png).

_capeVerdict: 2026-08-02, tools/char_intake.py on the first Tripo delivery. The swept-back cape FAILED to bind: cape panel A 85.9% arm-weighted, panel B 67.1% arm / 27.7% leg, at 7,714 and 6,789 verts (the largest sheet region on any shipped model is Vesper's collar at 1,610). Cause: an auto-rigger binds each vertex to the NEAREST joint, and the cape hung ~35 cm clear of the body, where nothing near it is the spine — under a stride it scissored with the limbs. The swept-back decision itself was VINDICATED in the same pass (arms separate closed loops at 42-52%, same as Finn; both hands 100% clean), so the fix is narrower than a redesign: keep the pose, keep the hood and the charcoal silhouette, close the garment against the body. All five shipped bodies wear coats and all five bind acceptably. Retired art: public/assets/characters/lake/turnaround-cape-retired/. NOTE, superseding an earlier line in this file: while the cape survived as a garment, the cut-ins deliberately drew it draped FORWARD (dramatic chest-up) while the turnaround swept it back (bindable) — one garment, two drapes, which is legitimate because a portrait never animates. That reasoning DIED with the cape. Lake now owns no cape at all, so a cape in a portrait is a plain continuity error and the cut-ins must be re-rolled to the open coat, not merely recoloured.
_lookNote: Identity ratified 2026-08-02 from public/assets/refs/lake.jpeg (user pick: base candidate 3). OPEN coat + FLAME-SCARLET vest are the user's 2026-08-02 picks: they chose the open-front silhouette on look, and asked for a flame colour in place of the green. Three temperatures were rendered (ember-orange, rust-red, flame-scarlet); the user picked SCARLET. My own recommendation had been ember-orange, on the grounds that it sits inside the golden-hour town palette while scarlet fights it — overruled, and the counter-argument I had recorded for scarlet is the one that matters more here: it reads at the town's 65 px character height, where a muted vest disappears.
_chainNote:
TWO SEPARATE CHAINS, AND CROSSING THEM IS A MISTAKE I MADE AND THE USER CAUGHT (2026-08-02).
  * THE 3D CHAIN: turnaround/front.png -> left/right/back -> Tripo. The A-pose is a 3D INPUT.
  * THE PORTRAIT CHAIN: bust.png -> bust-key.png -> cut-ins. Portraits descend from PORTRAITS.
I derived the bust FROM the A-pose, and it came back as a coloured-pencil rendering of a 3D model: stiff, doll-like, no warmth in the face. The user's words: 'the new bust.png style looks like it is downstream of the model, but we should have done this the other way around... We should have just transformed the clothes on bust-cape-superseded.png'. THE RULE: A GARMENT CHANGE IS A CLOTHING EDIT ON THE EXISTING PORTRAIT — keep the drawing, swap the cloth. Never anchor a portrait on the A-pose or anything derived from it.
Two measured constraints that survive from the same day, both instances of ONE law — THE REFERENCE IMAGE DICTATES SHAPE AND FRAMING, AND PROSE ARGUING WITH IT LOSES:
  (a) CROP. Asking for a 'half-body bust' while passing a full-body A-pose returned a full body; passing a chest-up CROP of that same A-pose returned a bust. Same finding the cut-in pipeline measured independently.
  (b) SILHOUETTE — SOLVED, and the solution is the general recipe for any future garment change. Editing the cape into a visibly-sleeved open coat failed 5 images across 3 rounds of PROSE, naming the sleeves explicitly every time: with one reference, the source garment's shape always won. I had recorded that as 'accepted'; the user rejected the compromise ('This seems like a real problem though since the whole reason we're redoing this is for the updated clothing style?') and they were right — a bust still wearing the old garment defeats the redesign.
    THE FIX IS TWO REFERENCES AT ONE FRAMING, WITH ROLES NAMED. Ref 1 = the existing PORTRAIT, owning style + face. Ref 2 = the A-pose CROPPED TO THE PORTRAIT'S OWN CROP, owning clothing only. The prompt says which reference owns what and says 'draw the second image's clothing on the first image's character, in the first image's style'. Sleeves appeared on the first attempt.
    Why this does not re-trigger the identity blend that burned this character twice: THAT failure came from refs at different FRAMINGS and different vintages. Same person, same framing, explicitly separated roles is a different operation. Do not generalise it to two refs of different crops.
  (c) STYLE. Rolls conditioned on a bust drifted to semi-photoreal ~7-head adults 4 times in 5; rolls chained off an already-on-model image held style AND identity 6 of 6. gen-character.mjs's TEXT-ONLY first link was bypassed on purpose — regenerating this face from prose returns a plausible stranger.
